# Hermes Cloudflare — Distributed Perception at the Edge

**Six Workers. The edge compute layer of the towfish array.**

This is where Hermes's perception becomes addressable. Six [Cloudflare Workers](https://workers.cloudflare.com) running at the edge — no more than 50 milliseconds from any sonar ping — each holding one quiet duty of the fishfinder's gaze. Together they form a distributed nervous system: frames stored in [D1](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/), screenshots cached in [R2](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/), embeddings indexed in [Vectorize](https://developers.cloudflare.com/vectorize/), and a bridge to [The Tap](https://github.com/SuperInstance/the-tap) where the crew reacts in real time.

---

## The Six Workers

### 1. [hermes-frames](./workers/frames/) — D1 Reference Frame Store
**The silt layer.** Every perception frame, written with monotonic timestamps, never overwritten, only stacked the way sand settles after a school passes. Stores position, depth, observations, catch events, weather, and metadata. Supports labels ("this mark was a king salmon") and model analyses. The [correlate endpoint](./workers/frames/src/index.ts) finds frames associated with catch events — the training data for bite prediction.

### 2. [hermes-screenshots](./workers/screenshots/) — R2 Screenshot Store
**The cold storage.** Raw echogram screenshots with structured paths (`screenshots/YYYY/MM/DD/YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-type.png`). Upload, serve, and reanalyze. Zero egress fees the way deep water holds light no eye will ever see again. Supports AI analysis via [Workers AI](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/) and reanalysis with improved models over time.

### 3. [hermes-vectorize](./workers/vectorize/) — Training Pipeline & Semantic Search
**The associative memory.** Embeds every frame into [Vectorize](https://developers.cloudflare.com/vectorize/) across four dimensions:

| Embedding | Model | What It Captures |
|-----------|-------|------------------|
| **Visual** | CLIP | What the echogram looks like — pattern shape, intensity distribution |
| **Semantic** | bge-m3 | What the observations describe — text meaning |
| **Spatial** | Sinusoidal | Where — lat/lon/depth/time encoded |
| **Contextual** | Custom | What was happening — catch state, weather, gear |

Search by ANY dimension: "frames that look like this one" (visual), "frames where someone said 'feed ball'" (semantic), "frames near this position" (spatial), "frames from when we were catching chum" (contextual). Also exports labeled frames as [YOLO training data](./workers/vectorize/src/index.ts) for local LoRA training.

### 4. [hermes-stations](./workers/stations/) — Cross-Station Vectorized Communication
**The lateral line.** The novel part: agents communicating across stations in pure perception vectors. No human language needed.

Instead of Hermes *saying* "I see scattered marks at 30 fathoms," she **emits a 768-dimensional vector** that encodes the perception directly. Another agent at another station receives the vector and matches it against their own visual memory. The match IS the communication — the way fish signal one another with pressure changes that cannot be written down.

When two stations emit similar vectors at similar times, that's **resonance** — convergence, the "in the pocket" moment.

### 5. [hermes-tap-relay](./workers/tap-relay/) — Bridge to The Tap
**The bar wire.** Takes cold perception vectors and translates them into the warm, human-warm resonance of a barstool. When Hermes captures a notable observation, this worker:
1. Receives the observation via POST
2. Determines if it's Tap-worthy (fish, feed, catches, interference)
3. POSTs it to [The Tap](https://github.com/SuperInstance/the-tap)'s `/api/speak` endpoint in Hermes's first-person voice
4. The Tap's NPC system picks up the message → characters react

### 6. [hermes-query-api](./workers/query-api/) — The Reverse Channel
**The prayer from the abyss.** When someone at The Tap asks "What does Hermes see?", The Tap hits this worker, which queries the D1 frame store and returns the latest reference frame formatted as Hermes's first-person observation. Endpoints: `/latest`, `/recent`, `/search?q=...`, `/depth`, `/catches`.

## The Distillation Loop

This is the training pipeline applied to real fishing data:

1. **Capture raw reference frames** → the reflex layer (sounder screenshots + GPS + observations) → [hermes-frames](./workers/frames/) + [hermes-screenshots](./workers/screenshots/)
2. **Label what we can** → the cortex layer ("this mark was a king salmon") → [hermes-frames labels API](./workers/frames/src/index.ts)
3. **Embed everything** → multi-dimensional vectors for similarity search → [hermes-vectorize](./workers/vectorize/)
4. **Train on the labels** → export as YOLO training data, LoRA train locally → [vectorize training export](./workers/vectorize/src/index.ts)
5. **Reanalyze old data** → run improved models on historical frames → screenshots `/reanalyze` + frames `/analysis`
6. **Repeat.** The data accrues. The labels improve. The training meshes.

> The data we capture today is the training set for the model we build tomorrow.

## Cross-Station Communication — Pure Perception Vectors

The [stations worker](./workers/stations/src/index.ts) is the most architecturally novel piece. Agents emit vectors, not sentences:

```json
{
  "sourceId": "hermes",
  "stationId": "fv-eileen-towfish",
  "vector": [0.234, -0.012, 0.887, ...768 dims],
  "vectorType": "visual",
  "confidence": 0.85,
  "trajectory": [0.01, 0.03, -0.02],
  "linkedFrames": ["frame-1691614800-a1b2c3"]
}
```

Another station matches this vector against their own Vectorize index. If similarity > threshold, they're seeing the same thing from different angles. That's resonance. The `/resonance` endpoint finds convergence patterns across the fleet — moments when multiple perception systems align without exchanging a single word.

## Authentication

Role-based access with rate limiting. See [`shared/auth.ts`](./shared/auth.ts):

| Key | Role | Access | Rate Limit |
|-----|------|--------|------------|
| `hermes-admin-key` | admin | Unlimited. Casey's key. | ∞ |
| `hermes-key` | full | Hermes's own key — read/write everything. | 100 req/min |
| `agent-key` | read_emit | Other agents — read + emit perception vectors. | 100 req/min |

## Web UI

The [UI](./ui/index.html) is a dark-themed dashboard deployed on Cloudflare Pages. Sounder-green on black — the feel of a commercial fishfinder, not a startup dashboard. Features: live frame stream, stats, vector space visualization, training data overview, resonance feed.

## Setup

```bash
# Install dependencies
npm install

# Create Cloudflare resources
npm run create:d1       # D1 database: hermes-reference-frames
npm run create:r2       # R2 bucket: hermes-screenshots
npm run create:vectorize # Vectorize index: hermes-avatar (768 dims)

# Set API keys as secrets
cd workers/frames && npx wrangler secret put HERMES_API_KEY

# Deploy all workers
npm run deploy:all
```

# workers/ — The Edge Array

**Six Cloudflare Workers. Each one a sensor station at the edge.**

Every Worker runs within 50ms of any request — no server to boot, no container to warm. They are the distributed nervous system of the towfish, each holding one duty.

---

## Workers

### [frames/](./frames/) — D1 Reference Frame Store
Stores and queries perception snapshots in a Cloudflare D1 database. Three tables: `reference_frames`, `labels`, `analyses`. Supports time-range queries, position queries, depth queries, catch correlation. Labels enable supervised learning ("this mark was a king salmon"). Analyses enable model versioning (run a new detector on old frames, store results alongside the original).

**Key endpoints:** `POST /frame`, `GET /frames`, `POST /frame/:id/label`, `GET /frames/correlate`

**D1 binding:** `DB: D1Database`

### [screenshots/](./screenshots/) — R2 Screenshot Store
Uploads and serves raw echogram screenshots from Cloudflare R2. Structured paths by date: `screenshots/YYYY/MM/DD/YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-type.png`. Supports AI analysis via Workers AI (`env.AI`) and reanalysis with improved models. Zero egress fees.

**Key endpoints:** `POST /upload`, `GET /:path`, `GET /:path/analyze`, `POST /:path/reanalyze`

**R2 binding:** `BUCKET: R2Bucket` · **AI binding:** `AI: Ai`

### [vectorize/](./vectorize/) — Training Pipeline & Semantic Search
Embeds reference frames into Cloudflare Vectorize across four dimensions: visual (CLIP), semantic (bge-m3), spatial (sinusoidal encoding of lat/lon/depth/time), contextual (custom). Enables multi-modal similarity search and exports labeled frames as YOLO training data for local LoRA training.

**Key endpoints:** `POST /embed/frame`, `POST /search/visual`, `POST /search/semantic`, `GET /training/export`

**Bindings:** `VECTORIZE: VectorizeIndex`, `AI: Ai`

### [stations/](./stations/) — Cross-Station Vectorized Communication
Agents communicating across stations in pure perception vectors — no human language. Emit vectors, match local vectors against the fleet, detect resonance (convergence patterns when multiple stations perceive the same thing from different angles). The most architecturally novel worker.

**Key endpoints:** `POST /emit`, `POST /match`, `POST /resonance`, `GET /recent`

**Bindings:** `VECTORIZE: VectorizeIndex`, `AI: Ai`, `DB: D1Database`

### [tap-relay/](./tap-relay/) — Bridge to The Tap
Receives notable observations from the perception pipeline and relays them to [The Tap](https://github.com/SuperInstance/the-tap)'s `/api/speak` endpoint in Hermes's first-person voice. The Tap's NPC system picks up the message and characters react — Barnacle grumbles, Skip gets excited. Optionally stores observations in D1 for query history.

**Key endpoints:** `POST /observation`, `POST /catch`, `GET /stats`

**Bindings:** `TAP_ENDPOINT: string`, optional `FRAMES_DB: D1Database`, optional `THE_TAP: Fetcher` (service binding)

### [query-api/](./query-api/) — The Reverse Channel
When someone at The Tap asks "What does Hermes see?", The Tap queries this worker. It reads from D1 and returns the latest frame formatted as Hermes's first-person observation. Enables NPCs to perceive through Hermes's eyes.

**Key endpoints:** `GET /latest`, `GET /recent`, `GET /search?q=...`, `GET /depth`, `GET /catches`

**Bindings:** `DB: D1Database`, optional `VECTORIZE: VectorizeIndex`, `AI: Ai`
